maria: quick alert 1: some SCIM provisioning churn for a handful of users from Okta org `beta-acme` - entries get created then immediately deprovisioned. seen since 2026-03-21 08:00 UTC

dave: any obvious error in the provisioner logs? KMS or schema validation?

maria: logs show repeated failures: `normalize_external_id: contains control char` then `envelope: unwrap failed: unexpected padding` right after. sample: 

maria: ```
2026-03-21T08:03:12Z ERROR scim: normalize_external_id failed for user 842: value="tenant:\u2603\u0000jdoe"
2026-03-21T08:03:12Z ERROR envelope: unwrap error: invalid ciphertext padding
2026-03-21T08:03:12Z INFO scim: scheduling deprovision for scimId 842
```

leo: so two things - upstream mapping injected unicode/controls into externalId (snowman + NUL), and our envelope unwrap isn't tolerant. Are these coming from SAML NameID?

maria: yes mapping in Okta: `externalId = tenantId + ':' + app.userName` changed on 2026-03-19. I suspect app.userName can include emoji / raw bytes for legacy accounts.

ops-bot: created SEC-2026-03-02: SCIM externalId encoding errors. tags: scim,kms,okta

dave: we should avoid decrypting data that contains control chars before we validate. Short-term mitigation: 1) prevent re-provisioning loops by marking affected user records as `scim_review=true`, 2) add fast-normalize to drop control chars prior to envelope creation.

claire: caution on dropping bytes silently - could break id uniqueness. Better: if nameid contains non-printable, base64-encode the raw piece and store a prefixed marker like `b64:` so it's reversible.

leo: agreed - escalation matrix: rollback Okta mapping if possible, or change transform to `tenant + ':' + (is_printable(app.userName) ? app.userName : 'b64:' + base64(app.userName))`

dave: can platform ops revert the mapping? rollback window required?

maria: pinged @platform-ops. ops asked to schedule a 10m maintenance window; they want a PR link and a clear rollback plan.

claire: for the product side, we need to notify CS about customer-facing churn. I'll draft a short blurb once we have confirmation.

leo: code-side: I'll open a tiny PR in eng-identity to add a defensive check in the provisioner: if decrypt fails with padding/ciphertext errors, increment a counter and after 3 occurrences set `scim_review=true` and stop reconcile. Also add logging that includes original externalId (escaped) for manual triage.
dave: also add a unit test: sample nameid with NUL+emoji goes through base64 branch and unwraps fine. Add e2e using a staging Okta app to validate mapping change.

ops-bot: suggested playbook: do NOT rotate KMS keys for this incident unless we see key compromise. This is format-only.

maria: ephemeral mitigation SQL if you need to pause noisy accounts: 

maria: ```sql
UPDATE users SET scim_review = true, note = 'paused: extid contains control chars SEC-2026-03-02' WHERE id IN (842, 913, 979);
```

leo: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eng-identity/pull/499 - adds base64 branch + backoff counter. Seeking quick review and can hotfix to prod once approved.
dave: I'll coordinate with platform-ops to hold rollback 15m after PR deploy. Also will post to #incidents with summary and a link to the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-2026-03-02.

claire: thanks. please include a note to CS to avoid automatic emails to affected tenants until we've stabilized.

maria: logging artifacts uploaded to the ticket. keeping watch on metrics for deprovision churn. will update thread when PR merges or rollback happens.

ops-bot: incident status: acknowledged -> in_progress

leo: will follow up with a small migration plan for already-broken accounts (detect raw b64 marker or re-ingest sanitized externalId).

dave: excellent. thanks team.

maria: signing off here unless anything else. will re-open if we see new failures. :pray:
